- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- If sentiment is rising (≥0.6) and price is trending up, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next period.
- Model frequently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish; apply 1–2% downward adjustment for first 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is volatile (rapid swings >0.25), model exhibits lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days and align with sentiment trend direction.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops after peak or rises after trough), model often fails to correct; apply 1–3% downward bias if sentiment is weak or neutral.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days show strong downward momentum, model tends to ignore it; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days unless sentiment is strong bullish.
